QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_27

question.text: Regarding side-letters with AIF investors, SEBI regulations broadly:

answer.text: Require SEBI approval for each side-letter individually
Impose restrictions on what additional rights can be granted via side-letters
Require all side-letters to be publicly disclosed on SEBI website

explanation.text: The Logic: The PDF states: 'there are restrictions within SEBI regulations on what can be given as an additional right in the side letter'. Side-letters are permitted but restricted — no economic favouritism, no terms that contradict the PPM's core economics, etc. The Trap: Outright prohibition is over-stated. Public disclosure / per-transaction SEBI approval are fictional procedures. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests side-letter regulation identically. Manager's Pro-Tip: The SEBI SFA implementation standards on side-letters (being finalised via IVCA forum) distinguish 'permissible' (reporting, co-invest access, fee) from 'impermissible' (preferential redemption, preferential fee tier). Keep your side-letter register up-to-date for CTR filing.
